composio.note: Composio manages OAuth for Box (OAUTH2), good for prototypes. A separate Box MCP toolkit (BOX_MCP) requires your own app.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio provides a managed Box app. For production, use your own app so users see your brand, get dedicated quota, and can use scopes beyond Composio's defaults.
reasons: Consent screen shows your app name instead of 'Composio'
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users; your own app gets dedicated quota
Managed apps use Composio's default scopes, which may not cover your needs
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval
The Box MCP toolkit requires your own app

prerequisites.title: Box developer or enterprise account
prerequisites.detail: A free developer account is enough to create an OAuth 2.0 app in the Developer Console.

prerequisites.title: Paid enterprise account for extra scopes
prerequisites.detail: Extra scopes cannot be requested on a free trial; log in to a paid enterprise account or upgrade first.

steps.title: Create the Box OAuth 2.0 app
steps.detail: Log into the Developer Console, select New App, choose User as app type, then Create.
steps.done_when: The app exists with a Client ID and secret.

steps.title: Choose scopes for the app
steps.detail: Draft the minimal scope list and select it in the Application Scopes section of the Configuration tab.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the Composio auth config with your own client ID and secret, then copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and Composio redirect URI is copied.

steps.title: Register redirect URI in Box
steps.detail: Add the Composio redirect URI under OAuth 2.0 Redirect URI on the Configuration page. It must be HTTPS and match exactly.
steps.done_when: The URI is saved in Box.

steps.title: Get customer admin enablement
steps.detail: Enterprise customers' admins may need to enable the app; the developer can submit an approval request from the Enablement tab, which emails the Primary Admin.

steps.title: Open support ticket for special scopes
steps.detail: Open a ticket via Box support naming the scope and use case. Agent can draft the justification.

steps.title: Submit app for Box Integrations listing
steps.detail: In Developer Console choose Apps, Submit for Approval, fill out the form and Submit.

traps.title: A newly created enterprise can authorize up to 10,000
traps.detail: A newly created enterprise can authorize up to 10,000 custom apps.

traps.title: Box uses user-based rate limits that generally trigger when
traps.detail: Box uses user-based rate limits that generally trigger when a user exceeds about 1000 API calls per minute, though certain endpoints may have different limits. The page does not say these limits differ for unreviewed apps.

traps.title: The upload limit is 240 file upload requests per
traps.detail: The upload limit is 240 file upload requests per minute per user.

traps.title: Box Sign limits are 100 create-and-resend sign request calls
traps.detail: Box Sign limits are 100 create-and-resend sign request calls per minute per user, and 1000 get-sign-request calls per minute per user.

traps.title: Scope changes need re-authorization
traps.detail: After changing scopes or access level, enterprise apps must be re-authorized by a Box Admin before changes take effect.

traps.title: Server apps need authorization
traps.detail: JWT and Client Credentials apps must be authorized before use, and an enterprise's Box Admin must approve them. An OAuth 2.0 app cannot be switched to Server type later.

traps.title: Missing redirect_uri parameter
traps.detail: If several redirect URIs are configured and the request omits redirect_uri, users see a redirect_uri_missing error.

traps.title: Composio callback domain cannot be verified by you
traps.detail: Box redirect URIs are an exact-match check, and Composio's callback domain is not yours. To use your own domain, proxy the callback through it with a 302 redirect.

traps.title: Customer API allocation
traps.detail: Calls from custom apps count toward each customer enterprise's monthly API allocation, unlike partner integrations.

blockers.symptom: Users cannot authorize the app; it appears inactive
blockers.what_it_means: The enterprise has the unpublished app inactive by default and needs an admin to enable it.
blockers.what_to_do: Give the customer's admin your Client ID, or submit an approval request from the Enablement tab.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the admin instructions and message.

blockers.symptom: Extra scope unavailable in the console
blockers.what_it_means: Scopes such as manage_legal_holds are available only through a support ticket.
blockers.what_to_do: Upgrade to a paid enterprise account and open a Box support ticket.

open_questions: How long does Box support take to approve special scope requests? Ask Box support or test with a ticket.
How long does the Box Integrations partner review take, and what does it check? See the Box Integrations page referenced by the docs.
How quickly do customer admins usually approve apps? Not documented; ask pilot customers.
Do unreviewed apps have lower rate limits? The docs do not say so; confirm with Box support.
